name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "His101 is the axial heme b ligand of gp91phox (CYBB). Replacing it with Arg removes the imidazole that coordinates the heme iron, so the heme cannot be held in the cytochrome b558 core and electron transfer from FAD to O2 fails.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E3", "E15", "E17", "E18", "E1", "E8", "E10", "E20"], "would_refute": "The His101 side chain in the heme-bound cryo-EM structures (8WEJ, 8X2L, 7U8G) is not within coordination distance (about 2.5 \u00c5) of the heme iron, or His101 is shown to be a non-coordinating residue. Equally, an Arg placed at 101 in a model that keeps the heme iron in place with a plausible ligand at the Arg position would weaken this hypothesis.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "UniProt annotates residue 101 as the axial heme b ligand (E3), and it is in the observed heme-bound structures (E15, E17, E18). This is the only evidence that ties the residue to a specific molecular function. It is still indirect: no paper or assay tests H101R (G1, G2, G4), and no structure carries the mutation (G3). Ranked above stability because E3 is residue-specific, while the stability evidence (E4, E8, E10, E11) only shows the residue is conserved and in a membrane helix."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "His101 sits in the transmembrane helix (residues 96-130) of gp91phox. Inserting a charged Arg into the membrane-embedded helix destabilises the four-helix cytochrome b558 fold, so the protein misfolds, is degraded, and fails to mature with p22phox.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E4", "E8", "E10", "E11", "E13", "E12", "E1"], "would_refute": "A stability calculation or MD run of the H101R model shows no significant destabilisation (for example ddG under about 1 kcal/mol, with the Arg side chain placed to avoid burial of charge). Or His101 is shown to be solvent-exposed and outside the membrane in the resolved structures, so it does not contribute to the helix packing.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Conservation (E10 0.952), popEVE (E11), EVE (E13) and AlphaMissense (E8) all predict the substitution is damaging, and the residue lies in a TM helix (E4). These scores do not say why the change is damaging, and they do not separate folding loss from heme loss. The folding route is supported by E12 (p22phox maturation depends on the complex) but no direct data exists for this residue (G2, G4). Ranked second because it explains the same predictions as H1 without a residue-specific function."}
